subject: Scott Colom
title: Who is Scott Colom? Mississippi Democrat in the 2026 Senate race
answer: Scott Colom is a Democrat and local prosecutor from Mississippi who is challenging Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith for a U.S. Senate seat in the 2026 midterm election. After the Nov. 3, 2026 vote he held a narrow lead of about 1,100 votes, but as of Nov. 5 the race had not been called and ballots were still being counted.
body:
Colom has been district attorney for Mississippi's 16th Judicial District, based in Lowndes County, since 2016. He won the Democratic primary with about 73% of the vote. Hyde-Smith, a Republican, was seeking a second full term. No Democrat has won a U.S. Senate seat in Mississippi in nearly four decades, and forecasters had rated the race safely Republican.

The result turned out far closer. Early on Nov. 4 Colom led by just 43 votes. By Wednesday night, Nov. 4, with about 96% of the expected vote counted, unofficial results showed Colom at 464,926 votes (49.0%), Hyde-Smith at 463,788 (48.9%) and independent Ty Pinkins at about 2.1%. No major outlet had called the race.

Thousands of ballots were still pending. Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day can arrive through Nov. 10; the Secretary of State's office said about 3,600 were outstanding. Affidavit (provisional) ballots are still being reviewed, and Colom's campaign estimated about 15,000 of them. Counties must certify results by Nov. 13. Mississippi has no runoff for this race, since the candidate with the most votes wins, and it has no automatic or requested recount; a losing candidate can examine ballot materials and challenge the result in court.
in_the_news: The Mississippi Senate race is one of the closest contests of the 2026 midterms. Colom led Hyde-Smith by about 1,100 votes on Nov. 4, with mail and affidavit ballots still to be counted.

faq.a: Not yet decided. As of Nov. 5, 2026, he led Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 1,100 votes in unofficial results, and the race was too close to call.

faq.q: When will the Mississippi Senate race be decided?
faq.a: Mail ballots can arrive through Nov. 10, and counties must certify results by Nov. 13. Affidavit ballots and any court challenge could push a final answer later.

faq.q: Is there a recount in Mississippi?
faq.a: Mississippi has no automatic or requested recount. After certification, a candidate can examine ballot materials and go to court if problems are found.

faq.q: Who is Scott Colom running against?
faq.a: Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, who has held the seat since 2018. Independent Ty Pinkins also ran and got about 2% of the vote.

faq.q: What job does Scott Colom have?
faq.a: He is district attorney for Mississippi's 16th Judicial District, a post he has held since 2016.
During the campaign he spoke about tariffs hurting Mississippians and about raising the minimum wage.
